summary_paragraph: Mr. Meléndez, a homeless man with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic alcohol and cocaine use, was admitted after being found unconscious on a bridge with altered mental status. He was somnolent on arrival, responded partially to Narcan, and had hypoglycemia and hypotension. Initial imaging showed no acute intracranial, cervical spine, or pulmonary pathology. He was managed for acute alcohol intoxication and at risk for withdrawal, for which he received prophylactic treatment. Acidosis improved with supportive care, and anemia was noted. He remained stable overnight, did not develop withdrawal symptoms, and was discharged the following morning with referrals for housing and cardiac follow-up.
